text:
Wall Go II · Securing territory on a 7×7 board · Three-player game followed by a two-player game

1. Setup and Victory
Round 1 is a three-player game. In the order determined by drawing lots, place one square counter and one round counter each on empty spaces of your choice.
The first placement proceeds in forward order, and the second placement proceeds in reverse order. Compete to survive and secure a larger territory.
Play proceeds without conversation, negotiation, or relationship ratings. At each choice, make your judgment based on the currently revealed board and your opponents' next moves.

2. Counter Movement
A square counter moves 1–2 spaces in one orthogonal direction: up, down, left, or right. A round counter moves one space up, down, left, or right, or
after moving one space, turns left or right and moves one more space. Moving 0 spaces or making a round trip back to the starting space is not allowed.
You cannot move onto a space occupied by another counter or jump over that counter, and you cannot pass through walls along your movement path.

3. Placing and Breaking Walls
On your turn, move one counter and then place exactly one wall on an empty edge among the top, bottom, left, and right edges of the destination space. Placing a wall is mandatory.
The board's outer boundary is already a wall, and you cannot place a wall over an existing wall. The time limit for each turn is 90 seconds.
If you exceed the time limit, any valid move is retained, but the wall is placed on a randomly selected available edge.
If the action format is invalid or the model-call budget is exhausted, play proceeds with the provided valid action.
Only in Round 1, each player may, once, break one wall blocking their movement path and move through it.
Once the region containing one of your counters is completely separated from other participants' counters, do not carry out unnecessary sequences of moves with that counter.
However, if a wall breaker remains and your region and a region of a different color are separated by a single wall,
you may also make preparatory moves and place walls to reach the position where you will break the wall.

4. Ending and Scoring
The game ends immediately once the regions containing each participant's counters are all separated, even if wall breakers remain.
Add up the number of cells in connected regions occupied only by you. Count each region only once, even if it contains several of your counters.
The game ends in a stalemate if no participant can make a valid move and place a wall.
In a stalemate, in regions where counters of different colors are trapped together, only the cell each counter currently occupies is recognized as a separate one-cell region.
Empty cells in mixed regions do not count toward anyone's score, and already separated regions occupied by only one participant are added up as usual.
If the totals are tied, compare the largest single region. If this value is also tied, only the tied participants replay, with their turn order reversed.
The first-place participant in Round 1 secures survival, and the other two proceed to Round 2.

5. Round 2
The participant who secured more territory in Round 1 goes first. Each participant uses 2 square counters and 2 round counters.
The first player's round counters are placed in fixed positions at (row,column) (2,2) and (6,6), and the second player's round counters at (2,6) and (6,2).
Place square counters in empty cells in the order first player, second player, second player, first player. There are no wall breakers.
In the event of a complete tie, replay with the first and second players switched. The loser of Round 2 is eliminated, and the two survivors each receive 1 Piece.

fields.note: P14 first places a square counter that can extend in all four directions from the center. After checking the opponent's placement, P14 can use the final round counter to target another region.

P02 secures a position that allows movement in multiple directions while maintaining distance from P14 in the center. This leaves room to place the second counter in another area after seeing the opponent's subsequent placement.
With P14 in the center and P02 in the upper left, claiming the lower-right corner first would make it easier to secure an independent region while maintaining distance from both opponents.

Since P03 has already placed the square counter in the lower right, P03 places the round counter in the opposite upper-right corner to increase the chances of securing territory in each of the two corners.

P02 places a square counter in the lower left to secure an area away from the existing round counter while leaving room to advance toward the center. The boundaries may change depending on P14's final placement.

Place a round counter at the bottom, away from the central square counter, to gain access to both regions. Look for an opportunity to separate territory in the center or at the bottom depending on the opponents' wall placements.

P14 judges that extending the wall along the right boundary will create an opportunity to constrict the space around P03's lower counter, while P14's own two counters can move in the center and at the bottom. No regions have been separated yet, and the opponents still have their wall breakers.

P02 creates a boundary facing P14 from a position close to the center, seeking an opportunity to secure space on the left. No regions have been separated yet, so P02 must check the opponent's next move.
Advance the square counter inward from the lower right and place a wall to the west to establish a foothold for securing the region on the right.

Extend the wall near the right boundary to create the possibility of constricting the space around P03's lower counter. No regions have been separated yet, and the opponents still have their wall breakers, so subsequent movements must be checked.
P02 extends the existing wall upward to form the boundary of the left region and preserves the wall breaker. No territory has been secured yet, so P02 needs to watch P14's movements in the center.

Move the square counter up to 4,7 to form a western boundary connecting to the existing walls in rows 5 and 6. This lays the groundwork for securing the right region while leaving room to connect with the round counter.

P14 moves the square counter closer to the right to respond to P03's territorial expansion while preserving the wall breaker. No region has been separated yet, so P14 will adjust the plan after seeing the opponent's next wall.

P02 checks P03's territorial expansion along the upper boundary and looks for an opportunity to secure the large central space. No region has been separated yet, so P02 needs to watch the opponent's next wall placement.

Move the square counter to 3,7 to extend the existing boundary wall in rows 4–6 up to row 3. This lays the groundwork for separating off a large section on the right while leaving the possibility of connecting with the round counter.

P14 moves the square counter toward the center while preserving the wall breaker. No territory has been secured yet, so P14 will adjust the next move after watching P03's blockade on the right and P02's movements.

P02 closes a gap in the right boundary to check P03's territorial expansion and preserves the wall breaker. However, P03 could secure territory by closing the remaining upper gap, so P02 needs to watch the next move.

Move the square counter to 2,7 and extend the wall along the existing right boundary to secure the right region containing both of P03's counters. Reduce routes that come into contact with opponents to improve the chances of survival.
Both of P03's counters are clustered in the upper right, but they are not yet completely separated. P14 narrows the right passage while preserving the wall breaker and watches the next move.
P02 confines both of P03's counters to two spaces, pressuring P03 to use the wall breaker. P03 could still break a wall and escape.
I will use the remaining wall breaker to enter 2,6 and block the boundary adjoining P02's round counter to protect P03's territory.

P14 looks for an opportunity to secure 3 spaces by closing the remaining entrance after the round counter enters the three spaces in the lower right. If the opponent's next wall changes the entrance, P14 will prioritize securing territory for the square counter.
P02 moves the isolated round counter out into a large region and blocks the passage toward P03's square counter. This uses the wall breaker but reduces the risk of being trapped in 1 space.

Move the square counter to 2,7 to connect it with the round counter, and block the route back to 2,6 to keep both counters together in a small region of their own. Prioritize the survival points that can be secured immediately.

P14 closes the last entrance to the three spaces in the lower right containing the round counter, securing 3 spaces. This exceeds P03's currently secured territory of 2 spaces, and all wall breakers have now been used up as well.

P02 places a wall in the central passage and leaves both counters in a large mixed region, aiming to secure territory later. Since P14 has already secured 3 spaces, P02 needs to check whether the central boundary closes on the next move.
P14 has already secured 3 spaces and is ahead of P03. P14 keeps the square counter in the spacious center to reduce the risk of immediate isolation and respond to P02's moves.

P02 secures the two spaces containing the round counter as an exclusive region to tie with P03, and continues pursuing a larger region with the square counter. Depending on P14's next move, P02 needs to examine the boundaries of the remaining mixed region.
P14 leads with 3 secured spaces but shares a large region with P02's square counter. P14 blocks P02's direct route to the right and aims for additional territory.
P02 moves the square counter into a large space near the center to pursue additional territory. P02 needs to check whether P14's next wall narrows the movement route.

P14 has secured 3 spaces, putting P14 1 space ahead of each opponent. P14 keeps the square counter in the center and narrows the connection toward P02, but additional territory is not yet guaranteed, so P14 watches the next move.
P02 keeps the square counter on the left and narrows the central boundary, looking for an opportunity to secure a larger region. P02 needs to check whether P14 blocks the lower passage.
P14 has already secured 3 spaces, putting P14 1 space ahead of each opponent. P14 keeps the square counter in the center, maintains movement routes, and watches P02's next wall.
P02 narrows the lower boundary while maintaining the passage leading to the large space on the left. P02 needs to watch whether P14, currently 1 point ahead, blocks the remaining alternate route.
P14 is 1 space ahead with 3 spaces but still shares a region with P02's square counter. P14 narrows the central connection while maintaining the square counter's movement route.
P02 stays in the left space and narrows the lower passage to pursue additional territory. P02 needs to watch whether P14 closes the remaining central connection.

P02 takes the center first to secure options for moving in all four directions and forming boundaries. After seeing the placement of the opponents' two square counters, P02 can use the final counter to reinforce a vulnerable side.
To counter P02's square counter in the center, take 3,4 first to secure movement options, choosing a position that can connect with the two fixed round counters.

Place the square counter at [3,5], which can connect to the upper-right area containing P03's round counter, to secure territory on that side while keeping a distance from P02's counter in the center.
P02 places a square counter in the lower-left area containing an opponent's round counter, seeking to contest territory on that side while also securing the option to move toward the center.

P02 forms a boundary in the center toward the opponent's square counter while maintaining a movement route to the right. No territory is secured yet, so P02 needs to watch whether the opponent's next wall divides the center.

Since P02's square counter has entered the center, move P03's square counter to [4,4] and block the boundary immediately beside it to curb the opponent's expansion. Also maintain the connection with the counters on the right.

P02 moves the square counter out of the position where two walls have restricted its movement, extending the boundary toward the opponent's counter in the center. No territory has been secured yet, so P02 must watch for the opponent blocking detour routes later.
Move P03's square counter to [3,6] to secure territory near the round counter at [2,6], and block [3,6]–[4,6] to strengthen the boundary with the center on P02's side.

P02 extends the central boundary to restrict the opponent's approach from the right while maintaining room for the square counter to move. No territory has been confirmed yet, so P02 must watch whether the opponent blocks the remaining detour routes.
Move P03's round counter to [2,5] and place a wall at [2,5]–[3,5] to extend the existing boundary. This choice reduces the routes through which P02's and P03's territories intermingle in the center.

P02 extends the right boundary to the edge of the board to restrict the opponent's access and aims to secure territory for the two lower counters. No territory has been confirmed yet, so P02 must watch for the opponent blocking detour routes.
Move P03's square counter to 3,7 and erect a wall at 3,7–4,7 to extend the boundary with P02's side toward 5,7. This choice increases the opportunity to secure the upper-right territory.

P02 blocks the space below the opponent's central square counter to restrict its movement while forming the boundary of the lower territory. No territory has been confirmed yet, so P02 must watch how the opponent uses the left passage.
Moving P03's square counter to [2,7] and blocking [2,7]–[3,7] will connect with the existing walls, narrowing the right passage and allowing P03 to defend the upper territory.

P02 extends the central boundary to the left to restrict the opponent's approach from the south and aims to secure the lower territory. No territory has been separated yet, so P02 must guard against the opponent's left detour route.
P03 lacks moves to connect the central boundary. Move the square counter to [3,4] and block [3,4]–[3,5], which connects to the existing walls, to check P02's expansion in the center.

P02 reduces the gaps in the left boundary to make it harder for the opponent to enter the lower area while aiming to secure a large territory. The territory has not been confirmed yet, so P02 must watch whether the opponent uses the remaining left passage.

P03 moves the square counter to [2,4] to block the direct passage from P02's round counter to the upper right. P03 places a wall to defend the upper territory before the opponent can take another route around.

P02 moves the round counter to the center to narrow the opponent's entry from the left while maintaining movement options. No territory has been confirmed yet, so P02 must check P03's next encircling move.

P03 can defend the upper-right territory while blocking the route by which P02's round counter could enter the upper area. Move square counter 2 to [2,6] and place a wall at [2,6]–[3,6] to extend the existing right boundary.
P02 blocks the central entry route while leaving room for the round counter to move left. P03's round counter is also in the lower area, so securing the territory is not assured.

Move P03's round counter to [1,5] to extend the wall running through [2,5]–[3,5] and [3,5]–[4,5] to the upper boundary. This choice protects P03's counter in the upper right and prevents its territory from intermingling with that of P02's lower counters.

P02 closes off the left boundary, cutting the connection between the upper and lower sections and restricting the opponent's movement. Both regions still contain opposing counters, so the points are not yet secured, and the next enclosing move needs to be examined.
P03 moves square counter 1 to [2,5] and blocks [2,4]–[2,5]. This can separate the counters and region in the upper right from P02's central counter.

P02 moves a square counter out of the corner and establishes a boundary against the opponent's round counter to reduce the risk of being surrounded. The lower region still contains counters from both players, so the opponent's next wall needs to be checked.
P03 groups the upper counters into one region while extending the existing wall upward to secure the upper right. This choice reduces the routes P02 could use to enter by going around from below.
P02 moves the central round counter, which has only one exit, to reduce the risk of being surrounded. P02 builds a wall in the left passage, but the region and points are not yet secured.
P03 moves square counter 1 to [2,6] and blocks [2,6]–[2,7]. By connecting this to the existing right boundary, P03 narrows the passage through which P02 could enter the upper right.

P02 blocks one passage in the lower left, where the opponent's round counter is located, aiming to separate the region. The opponent still has another movement route, so the secured points have not yet been determined.

While protecting the existing 2-cell region in the upper right, blocking between [1,7] and [2,7] increases the possibility of securing one more cell. The boundaries around the other counters are still open, so how much the region will expand remains uncertain.

P02 moves the square counter that could become isolated on the next turn out of (5,1) and narrows the upper entry route for the opponent's round counter. The opponent may still use the remaining lower passage.
P03 moves a round counter to [2,4] and extends the wall along [2,4]–[3,4]. This choice aims to enlarge the upper region by extending the existing boundary and prevent P02 from entering the center.

P02 narrows the passage between the opponent's lower counter and P02's own counter on the right, aiming to secure a large region. Other passages are still open, so the opponent's next blocking move needs to be examined.
P03 moves square counter 2 to [1,6] and blocks the western boundary, aiming to secure both upper cells, which are already blocked below. This choice could enlarge the region currently worth 2 points.
P02 narrows the lower passage, seeking an opportunity to secure the large region on the right. P03 could separate the lower-left region and score points, so the next wall needs to be examined.

The central passage where P02's counters are gathered is narrowed further to check the opponent's territorial expansion. This protects the 4 points already secured while leaving room to secure the lower region.

P02 separates the lower left, where the opponent's round counter is located, into a 5-cell region while leaving P02's own round counter outside. The opponent's secured points increase, but an opportunity remains to secure the remaining large region.
P02 is leading with 19 points, so a move is needed to secure more territory for P03 and block the opponent's entry. Blocking [1,4]–[2,4] extends the existing boundary upward.

P02 leads 19 to 9, so they place the round counter on the larger side of the mixed region and narrow the opponent's upper entry route. Even if the opponent blocks the remaining passage, the total secured territory is what matters.
Enter [2,3] and block the boundary with P02's counter as the move most likely to reduce P02's 19-point territory. Keep the 9 points already secured while challenging the opponent's advantage.

P02 leads 19 to 9, so they move the round counter toward the larger region and restrict the opponent's access. The remaining upper connection will be adjudicated depending on the opponent's next move.
Currently far behind with 9 points, choose a move that can secure more of the upper region. From [1,3], block [1,3]–[1,4] to connect to and reinforce the existing boundary.
P02 leads 19 to 9 and blocks the opponent's central entry route in the upper mixed region. The opponent still has a passage on the left, so whether further separation occurs must be monitored.

P02 is ahead with 19 points, so a move to block the central entry route is needed. Move the round counter to [2,3] and close the southern boundary to protect the secured territory while checking P02's expansion.
P02 leads 19 to 9, places the round counter in the center, and narrows the upper-left connection. Any additional territory resulting from the opponent's next wall has not yet been determined.
P03 closes the lower boundary of [1,3] to reinforce the upper region connected to the existing walls and tries to prevent entry by P02, who leads with 19 points.

P02 can secure additional territory by closing the upper connection while leaving their round counter on the opposite side. This also gives the opponent territory, but it is advantageous for maintaining the current 19-to-9 gap.
